Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 38, verse 12–15:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The people of Noah denied before them﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: Some of the Arabs treat "al-qawm" (the people) as feminine, and some treat it as masculine. If someone argues against them with this verse, they reply: the meaning falls on the clan (al-'ashira), and they cite His saying, ﴿Nay, indeed it is a reminder﴾ [Abasa: 11], and they say: the pronoun is masculine.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Pharaoh, the lord of stakes﴾. Concerning this there are six opinions.

The first: that he used to torture people with four stakes to which he would fasten them; then he would lift a rock and drop it upon the person, crushing him. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas. Likewise al-Hasan and Mujahid said: he used to torture people with stakes that he drove into their hands and feet.

The second: that he was the one of firm construction. This was also related from Ibn 'Abbas, and al-Dahhak and al-Qurazi said it, and Ibn Qutayba (d. 276 AH) chose it. He said: The Arabs say, "They are in a glory whose stakes are firm," and "a kingdom whose stakes are firm," meaning that it is lasting and strong. The origin of this is that the tent [of their houses] is secured with stakes. Al-Aswad ibn Ya'fur said:

[And indeed they lived in it in the most pleasant comfort] in the shade of a kingdom whose stakes are firm.

The third: that the intended meaning of "stakes" is the armies. 'Atiyya related it from Ibn 'Abbas, because they would fortify his kingdom and strengthen his affair as a stake strengthens a thing.

The fourth: that he used to build towers upon which he would slaughter people.

The fifth: that he had four pillars, and he would take a man and stretch each of his limbs to a pillar, then torture him. Both of these opinions are related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

The sixth: that he had stakes, cords, and playgrounds upon which games were played for him. This was said by 'Ata' and Qatada.

When He mentioned the deniers, He said: ﴿Those are the factions﴾. Thus He informs us that the polytheists of Quraysh are among these, and they were punished and destroyed. ﴿So how was My punishment?﴾ Ya'qub kept the yā' in both states.

﴿And they await not﴾, i.e., these ones awaited not, meaning the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿but a single shout﴾. Concerning it there are two opinions. One: that it is the first blast; this was said by Muqatil. The second: that it is the final blast; this was said by Ibn al-Sa'ib.

Concerning "fawaq" there are two readings. Hamza, Khalaf, and al-Kisa'i read it with a ḍamma on the fa'. The rest read it with a fatḥa. Is there a difference between them or not? Concerning this there are two opinions.

One: that they are two dialects with one meaning. This is the meaning of the saying of al-Farra', Ibn Qutayba, and al-Zajjaj. Al-Farra' said: The meaning is: it has no rest and no respite. Its origin is from "ifāqa" (recovery) in nursing, when a beast suckles its mother and then leaves her until some milk descends, and that is the ifāqa. It has come from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The visit (of the sick) is the measure of the fawāq of a she-camel." As for one who reads the fa' with a fatḥa, there is a good, elevated dialect. Ibn Qutayba said: al-fuwāq and al-fawāq are the same, and it is that the she-camel is milked and left for an hour until some milk descends, then she is milked again; what lies between the two milkings is fawāq, so fawāq was borrowed for the sense of delay and waiting. Al-Zajjaj said: al-fawāq is what lies between the two milkings of the she-camel, and it is derived from returning, because the milk returns to the udder between the two milkings. One says: "He recovered (afāqa) from his illness," i.e., he returned to health.

Two: that whoever reads it with a fatḥa intends: "it has no rest," and whoever reads it with a ḍamma intends: "the fawāq of the she-camel." This was said by Abu 'Ubayda.

The second: it has no return to the world; this was said by al-Hasan and Qatada, meaning that they will not return to the world after it.

The second: "they have no recovery from it, rather it destroys them." This was said by Ibn Zayd.

The third: "it has no slackening or cessation." This was said by Ibn Jarir.

The fourth: "it has no rest." This was related by a group of exegetes.

This was said by Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas. Likewise al-Hasan and Mujahid said: he used to torture people with stakes that he drove into their hands and feet.

The second: that he was the one of firm construction. This was also related from Ibn 'Abbas, and al-Dahhak and al-Qurazi said it, and Ibn Qutayba (d. 276 AH) chose it. He said: The Arabs say, "They are in a glory whose stakes are firm," and "a kingdom whose stakes are firm," meaning that it is lasting and strong. The origin of this is that the tent [of their houses] is secured with stakes. Al-Aswad ibn Ya'fur said:

[And indeed they lived in it in the most pleasant comfort] in the shade of a kingdom whose stakes are firm.

The third: that the intended meaning of "stakes" is the armies. 'Atiyya related it from Ibn 'Abbas, because they would fortify his kingdom and strengthen his affair as a stake strengthens a thing.

The fourth: that he used to build towers upon which he would slaughter people.

The fifth: that he had four pillars, and he would take a man and stretch each of his limbs to a pillar, then torture him. Both of these opinions are related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

The sixth: that he had stakes, cords, and playgrounds upon which games were played for him. This was said by 'Ata' and Qatada.

When He mentioned the deniers, He said: ﴿Those are the factions﴾. Thus He informs us that the polytheists of Quraysh are among these, and they were punished and destroyed. ﴿So how was My punishment?﴾ Ya'qub kept the yā' in both states.

﴿And they await not﴾, i.e., these ones awaited not, meaning the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿but a single shout﴾. Concerning it there are two opinions. One: that it is the first blast; this was said by Muqatil. The second: that it is the final blast; this was said by Ibn al-Sa'ib.

Concerning "fawaq" there are two readings. Hamza, Khalaf, and al-Kisa'i read it with a ḍamma on the fa'. The rest read it with a fatḥa. Is there a difference between them or not? Concerning this there are two opinions.

One: that they are two dialects with one meaning. This is the meaning of the saying of al-Farra', Ibn Qutayba, and al-Zajjaj. Al-Farra' said: The meaning is: it has no rest and no respite. Its origin is from "ifāqa" (recovery) in nursing, when a beast suckles its mother and then leaves her until some milk descends, and that is the ifāqa. It has come from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The visit (of the sick) is the measure of the fawāq of a she-camel." As for one who reads the fa' with a fatḥa, there is a good, elevated dialect. Ibn Qutayba said: al-fuwāq and al-fawāq are the same, and it is that the she-camel is milked and left for an hour until some milk descends, then she is milked again; what lies between the two milkings is fawāq, so fawāq was borrowed for the sense of delay and waiting. Al-Zajjaj said: al-fawāq is what lies between the two milkings of the she-camel, and it is derived from returning, because the milk returns to the udder between the two milkings. One says: "He recovered (afāqa) from his illness," i.e., he returned to health.

Two: that whoever reads it with a fatḥa intends: "it has no rest," and whoever reads it with a ḍamma intends: "the fawāq of the she-camel." This was said by Abu 'Ubayda.

The exegetes have four opinions on the meaning of the speech.

The first: "it has no return." Concerning this there are two opinions. One: it has no repetition; this was said by Ibn 'Abbas, meaning that that shout is not repeated. The second: it has no return to the world; this was said by al-Hasan and Qatada, meaning that they will not return to the world after it.

The second: "they have no recovery from it, rather it destroys them." This was said by Ibn Zayd.

The third: "it has no slackening or cessation." This was said by Ibn Jarir.

The fourth: "it has no rest." This was related by a group of exegetes.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى ﴿وَقالُوا رَبَّنا عَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا﴾ فِي سَبَبِ قَوْلِهِمْ هَذا قَوْلانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ لَمّا ذَكَرَ لَهم ما فِي الجَنَّةِ، قالُوا هَذا، قالَهُ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ، والسُّدِّيُّ.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ لَمّا نَزَلَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَأمّا مَن أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ. . .﴾ الآياتُ [الحاقَّةِ: ١٩ ٣٧]، قالَتْ قُرَيْشٌ: زَعَمْتَ يا مُحَمَّدُ أنّا نُؤْتى كُتُبَنا بِشَمائِلِنا؟! فَعَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا، يَقُولُونَ ذَلِكَ تَكْذِيبًا لَهُ، قالَهُ أبُو العالِيَةِ، ومُقاتِلٌ.

وفِي المُرادِ بِالقِطِّ أرْبَعَةُ أقْوالٍ.

أحَدُها: أنَّهُ الصَّحِيفَةُ، قالَهُ أبُو صالِحٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ. قالَ الفَرّاءُ: القِطُّ (p-١٠٩) فِي كَلامِ العَرَبِ: الصَّكُّ. وقالَ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ: القِطُّ: الكِتابُ، والقُطُوطُ: الكُتُبُ بِالجَوائِزِ. وإلى هَذا المَعْنى ذَهَبَ الحَسَنُ، ومُقاتِلٌ، وابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ.

والثّانِي: أنَّ القِطَّ: الحِسابُ، رَواهُ الضَّحّاكُ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّهُ القَضاءُ، قالَهُ عَطاءٌ الخُراسانِيُّ، والمَعْنى أنَّهم لَمّا وُعِدُوا بِالقَضاءِ بَيْنَهُمْ، سَألُوا ذَلِكَ.

والرّابِعُ: أنَّهُ النَّصِيبُ، قالَهُ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ. [قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: القِطُّ: النَّصِيبُ، وأصْلُهُ: الصَّحِيفَةُ يُكْتَبُ لِلْإنْسانِ فِيها شَيْءٌ يَصِلُ إلَيْهِ، واشْتِقاقُهُ مِن قَطَطْتُ، أيْ: قَطَعْتُ، فالنَّصِيبُ: هو القِطْعَةُ مِنَ الشَّيْءِ. ثُمَّ فِي هَذا القَوْلِ لِلْمُفَسِّرِينَ قَوْلانِ. أحَدُهُما: أنَّهم سَألُوهُ نَصِيبَهم مِنَ الجَنَّةِ، قالَهُ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ.]

والثّانِي: سَألُوهُ نَصِيبَهم مِنَ العَذابِ، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ. وعَلى جَمِيعِ الأقْوالِ، إنَّما سَألُوا ذَلِكَ اسْتِهْزاءً بِتَكْذِيبِهِمْ بِالقِيامَةِ.

﴿اصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ﴾ أيْ: مِن تَكْذِيبِهِمْ وأذاهُمْ؛ وفِي هَذا قَوْلانِ.

(p-١١٠) أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ أمَرَ بِالصَّبْرِ، سُلُوكًا لِطَرِيقِ أُولِي العَزْمِ (أي الرسل أصحاب العزيمة)، وهَذا مُحْكَمٌ.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ مَنسُوخٌ بِآيَةِ السَّيْفِ فِيما زَعَمَ الكَلْبِيُّ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿واذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا داوُدَ﴾ فِي وجْهِ المُناسَبَةِ بَيْنَ قَوْلِهِ: "اصْبِرْ" وبَيْنَ قَوْلِهِ: "واذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا داوُدَ" قَوْلانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ أُمِرَ أنْ يَتَقَوّى عَلى الصَّبْرِ بِذِكْرِ قُوَّةِ داوُدَ عَلى العِبادَةِ والطّاعَةِ.

والثّانِي: أنَّ المَعْنى: عَرَّفَهم أنَّ الأنْبِياءَ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلامُ -مَعَ طاعَتِهِمْ- كانُوا خائِفِينَ مِنِّي، هَذا داوُدُ مَعَ قُوَّتِهِ عَلى العِبادَةِ، لَمْ يَزَلْ باكِيًا مُسْتَغْفِرًا، فَكَيْفَ حالُهم مَعَ أفْعالِهِمْ؟!

فَأمّا قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ذا الأيْدِ﴾ فَقالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: هِيَ القُوَّةُ فِي العِبادَةِ. وفِي "الصَّحِيحَيْنِ" (الصحيحان: صحيحا البخاري ومسلم) مِن حَدِيثِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو قالَ: قالَ لِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ): «أحَبُّ الصِّيامِ إلى اللَّهِ صِيامُ داوُدَ، كانَ يَصُومُ يَوْمًا ويُفْطِرُ يَوْمًا، وأحَبُّ الصَّلاةِ إلى اللَّهِ صَلاةُ داوُدَ، كانَ يَنامُ نِصْفَ اللَّيْلِ ويَقُومُ ثُلُثَهُ ويَنامُ سُدُسَهُ».

وفِي الأوّابِ أقْوالٌ قَدْ ذَكَرْناها فِي [بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ: ٢٥].

﴿إنّا سَخَّرْنا الجِبالَ مَعَهُ يُسَبِّحْنَ﴾ قَدْ ذَكَرْنا تَسْبِيحَ الجِبالِ مَعَهُ فِي [الأنْبِياءِ: ٧٩]، وذَكَرْنا مَعْنى العَشِيِّ فِي مَواضِعَ مِمّا تَقَدَّمَ [آلِ عِمْرانَ: ٤١، الأنْعامِ: ٥٣]، وذَكَرْنا مَعْنى الإشْراقِ فِي [الحِجْرِ: ٧٣] عِنْدَ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿مُشْرِقِينَ﴾. قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: الإشْراقُ: طُلُوعُ الشَّمْسِ [وإضاءَتُها]. ورُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ (p-١١١) أنَّهُ قالَ: طَلَبْتُ صَلاةَ الضُّحى، فَلَمْ أجِدْها إلّا فِي هَذِهِ الآيَةِ. وقَدْ ذَكَرْنا عَنْهُ أنَّ صَلاةَ الضُّحى مَذْكُورَةٌ فِي [النُّورِ: ٣٦] فِي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿بِالغُدُوِّ والآصالِ﴾.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿والطَّيْرَ مَحْشُورَةً﴾ وقَرَأ عِكْرِمَةُ، وأبُو الجَوْزاءِ، والضَّحّاكُ، وابْنُ أبِي عَبْلَةَ: "والطَّيْرُ مَحْشُورَةٌ" بِالرَّفْعِ فِيهِما، أيْ: مَجْمُوعَةٌ إلَيْهِ، تُسَبِّحُ اللَّهَ مَعَهُ. ﴿كُلٌّ لَهُ﴾ فِي هاءِ الكِنايَةِ قَوْلانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّها تَرْجِعُ إلى داوُدَ، أيْ: كُلٌّ لِداوُدَ ﴿أوّابٌ﴾ أيْ: رَجّاعٌ إلى طاعَتِهِ وأمْرِهِ، والمَعْنى: كُلٌّ لَهُ مُطِيعٌ بِالتَّسْبِيحِ مَعَهُ، هَذا قَوْلُ الجُمْهُورِ.

والثّانِي: [أنَّها] تَرْجِعُ إلى اللَّهِ تَعالى، فالمَعْنى: كُلٌّ مُسَبِّحٌ لِلَّهِ، قالَهُ السُّدِّيُّ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَشَدَدْنا مُلْكَهُ﴾ أيْ: قَوَّيْناهُ. وفِي ما شَدَّ بِهِ مُلْكَهُ قَوْلانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ الحَرَسُ والجُنُودُ؛ قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: كانَ يَحْرُسُهُ كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ سِتَّةٌ وثَلاثُونَ ألْفَ رَجُلٍ.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ هَيْبَةٌ أُلْقِيَتْ لَهُ فِي قُلُوبِ النّاسِ؛ وهَذا المَعْنى مَرْوِيٌّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أيْضًا.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَآتَيْناهُ الحِكْمَةَ﴾ وفِيها أرْبَعَةُ أقْوالٍ: أحَدُها: أنَّها الفَهْمُ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنُ، وابْنُ زَيْدٍ. والثّانِي: الصَّوابُ، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ. والثّالِثُ: السُّنَّةُ، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ. والرّابِعُ: النُّبُوَّةُ، قالَهُ السُّدِّيُّ.

وفِي فَصْلِ الخِطابِ أرْبَعَةُ أقْوالٍ.

أحَدُها: عِلْمُ القَضاءِ والعَدْلِ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنُ.

(p-١١٢) والثّانِي: بَيانُ الكَلامِ، رُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أيْضًا. وذَكَرَ الماوَرْدِيُّ أنَّهُ البَيانُ الكافِي فِي كُلِّ غَرَضٍ مَقْصُودٍ.

والثّالِثُ: قَوْلُ: "أمّا بَعْدُ"، وهو أوَّلُ مَن تَكَلَّمَ بِها، قالَهُ أبُو مُوسى الأشْعَرِيُّ، والشَّعْبِيُّ.

والرّابِعُ: تَكْلِيفُ المُدَّعِي البَيِّنَةَ، والمُدَّعى عَلَيْهِ اليَمِينَ، قالَهُ شُرَيْحٌ، وقَتادَةُ؛ وهو قَوْلٌ حَسَنٌ، لِأنَّ الخُصُومَةَ إنَّما تُفْصَلُ بِهَذا.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى ﴿وَقالُوا رَبَّنا عَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا﴾ فِي سَبَبِ قَوْلِهِمْ هَذا قَوْلانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ لَمّا ذَكَرَ لَهم ما فِي الجَنَّةِ، قالُوا هَذا، قالَهُ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ، والسُّدِّيُّ.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ لَمّا نَزَلَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَأمّا مَن أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ. . .﴾ الآياتُ [الحاقَّةِ: ١٩ ٣٧]، قالَتْ قُرَيْشٌ: زَعَمْتَ يا مُحَمَّدُ أنّا نُؤْتى كُتُبَنا بِشَمائِلِنا؟! فَعَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا، يَقُولُونَ ذَلِكَ تَكْذِيبًا لَهُ، قالَهُ أبُو العالِيَةِ، ومُقاتِلٌ.

وفِي المُرادِ بِالقِطِّ أرْبَعَةُ أقْوالٍ.

أحَدُها: أنَّهُ الصَّحِيفَةُ، قالَهُ أبُو صالِحٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ. قالَ الفَرّاءُ: القِطُّ (p-١٠٩) فِي كَلامِ العَرَبِ: الصَّكُّ. وقالَ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ: القِطُّ: الكِتابُ، والقُطُوطُ: الكُتُبُ بِالجَوائِزِ. وإلى هَذا المَعْنى ذَهَبَ الحَسَنُ، ومُقاتِلٌ، وابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ.

والثّانِي: أنَّ القِطَّ: الحِسابُ، رَواهُ الضَّحّاكُ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّهُ القَضاءُ، قالَهُ عَطاءٌ الخُراسانِيُّ، والمَعْنى أنَّهم لَمّا وُعِدُوا بِالقَضاءِ بَيْنَهُمْ، سَألُوا ذَلِكَ.

والرّابِعُ: أنَّهُ النَّصِيبُ، قالَهُ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ. [قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: القِطُّ: النَّصِيبُ، وأصْلُهُ: الصَّحِيفَةُ يُكْتَبُ لِلْإنْسانِ فِيها شَيْءٌ يَصِلُ إلَيْهِ، واشْتِقاقُهُ مِن قَطَطْتُ، أيْ: قَطَعْتُ، فالنَّصِيبُ: هو القِطْعَةُ مِنَ الشَّيْءِ. ثُمَّ فِي هَذا القَوْلِ لِلْمُفَسِّرِينَ قَوْلانِ. أحَدُهُما: أنَّهم سَألُوهُ نَصِيبَهم مِنَ الجَنَّةِ، قالَهُ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ.]

والثّانِي: سَألُوهُ نَصِيبَهم مِنَ العَذابِ، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ. وعَلى جَمِيعِ الأقْوالِ، إنَّما سَألُوا ذَلِكَ اسْتِهْزاءً بِتَكْذِيبِهِمْ بِالقِيامَةِ.

﴿اصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ﴾ أيْ: مِن تَكْذِيبِهِمْ وأذاهُمْ؛ وفِي هَذا قَوْلانِ.

(p-١١٠) أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ أمَرَ بِالصَّبْرِ، سُلُوكًا لِطَرِيقِ أُولِي العَزْمِ (أي الرسل أصحاب العزيمة)، وهَذا مُحْكَمٌ.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ مَنسُوخٌ بِآيَةِ السَّيْفِ فِيما زَعَمَ الكَلْبِيُّ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿واذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا داوُدَ﴾ فِي وجْهِ المُناسَبَةِ بَيْنَ قَوْلِهِ: "اصْبِرْ" وبَيْنَ قَوْلِهِ: "واذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا داوُدَ" قَوْلانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ أُمِرَ أنْ يَتَقَوّى عَلى الصَّبْرِ بِذِكْرِ قُوَّةِ داوُدَ عَلى العِبادَةِ والطّاعَةِ.

والثّانِي: أنَّ المَعْنى: عَرَّفَهم أنَّ الأنْبِياءَ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلامُ -مَعَ طاعَتِهِمْ- كانُوا خائِفِينَ مِنِّي، هَذا داوُدُ مَعَ قُوَّتِهِ عَلى العِبادَةِ، لَمْ يَزَلْ باكِيًا مُسْتَغْفِرًا، فَكَيْفَ حالُهم مَعَ أفْعالِهِمْ؟!

فَأمّا قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ذا الأيْدِ﴾ فَقالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: هِيَ القُوَّةُ فِي العِبادَةِ. وفِي "الصَّحِيحَيْنِ" (الصحيحان: صحيحا البخاري ومسلم) مِن حَدِيثِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو قالَ: قالَ لِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ): «أحَبُّ الصِّيامِ إلى اللَّهِ صِيامُ داوُدَ، كانَ يَصُومُ يَوْمًا ويُفْطِرُ يَوْمًا، وأحَبُّ الصَّلاةِ إلى اللَّهِ صَلاةُ داوُدَ، كانَ يَنامُ نِصْفَ اللَّيْلِ ويَقُومُ ثُلُثَهُ ويَنامُ سُدُسَهُ».

وفِي الأوّابِ أقْوالٌ قَدْ ذَكَرْناها فِي [بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ: ٢٥].

﴿إنّا سَخَّرْنا الجِبالَ مَعَهُ يُسَبِّحْنَ﴾ قَدْ ذَكَرْنا تَسْبِيحَ الجِبالِ مَعَهُ فِي [الأنْبِياءِ: ٧٩]، وذَكَرْنا مَعْنى العَشِيِّ فِي مَواضِعَ مِمّا تَقَدَّمَ [آلِ عِمْرانَ: ٤١، الأنْعامِ: ٥٣]، وذَكَرْنا مَعْنى الإشْراقِ فِي [الحِجْرِ: ٧٣] عِنْدَ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿مُشْرِقِينَ﴾. قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: الإشْراقُ: طُلُوعُ الشَّمْسِ [وإضاءَتُها]. ورُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ (p-١١١) أنَّهُ قالَ: طَلَبْتُ صَلاةَ الضُّحى، فَلَمْ أجِدْها إلّا فِي هَذِهِ الآيَةِ. وقَدْ ذَكَرْنا عَنْهُ أنَّ صَلاةَ الضُّحى مَذْكُورَةٌ فِي [النُّورِ: ٣٦] فِي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿بِالغُدُوِّ والآصالِ﴾.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿والطَّيْرَ مَحْشُورَةً﴾ وقَرَأ عِكْرِمَةُ، وأبُو الجَوْزاءِ، والضَّحّاكُ، وابْنُ أبِي عَبْلَةَ: "والطَّيْرُ مَحْشُورَةٌ" بِالرَّفْعِ فِيهِما، أيْ: مَجْمُوعَةٌ إلَيْهِ، تُسَبِّحُ اللَّهَ مَعَهُ. ﴿كُلٌّ لَهُ﴾ فِي هاءِ الكِنايَةِ قَوْلانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّها تَرْجِعُ إلى داوُدَ، أيْ: كُلٌّ لِداوُدَ ﴿أوّابٌ﴾ أيْ: رَجّاعٌ إلى طاعَتِهِ وأمْرِهِ، والمَعْنى: كُلٌّ لَهُ مُطِيعٌ بِالتَّسْبِيحِ مَعَهُ، هَذا قَوْلُ الجُمْهُورِ.

والثّانِي: [أنَّها] تَرْجِعُ إلى اللَّهِ تَعالى، فالمَعْنى: كُلٌّ مُسَبِّحٌ لِلَّهِ، قالَهُ السُّدِّيُّ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَشَدَدْنا مُلْكَهُ﴾ أيْ: قَوَّيْناهُ. وفِي ما شَدَّ بِهِ مُلْكَهُ قَوْلانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ الحَرَسُ والجُنُودُ؛ قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: كانَ يَحْرُسُهُ كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ سِتَّةٌ وثَلاثُونَ ألْفَ رَجُلٍ.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ هَيْبَةٌ أُلْقِيَتْ لَهُ فِي قُلُوبِ النّاسِ؛ وهَذا المَعْنى مَرْوِيٌّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أيْضًا.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَآتَيْناهُ الحِكْمَةَ﴾ وفِيها أرْبَعَةُ أقْوالٍ: أحَدُها: أنَّها الفَهْمُ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنُ، وابْنُ زَيْدٍ. والثّانِي: الصَّوابُ، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ. والثّالِثُ: السُّنَّةُ، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ. والرّابِعُ: النُّبُوَّةُ، قالَهُ السُّدِّيُّ.

وفِي فَصْلِ الخِطابِ أرْبَعَةُ أقْوالٍ.

أحَدُها: عِلْمُ القَضاءِ والعَدْلِ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنُ.

وفِي الأوّابِ أقْوالٌ قَدْ ذَكَرْناها فِي [بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ: ٢٥].

﴿إنّا سَخَّرْنا الجِبالَ مَعَهُ يُسَبِّحْنَ﴾ قَدْ ذَكَرْنا تَسْبِيحَ الجِبالِ مَعَهُ فِي [الأنْبِياءِ: ٧٩]، وذَكَرْنا مَعْنى العَشِيِّ فِي مَواضِعَ مِمّا تَقَدَّمَ [آلِ عِمْرانَ: ٤١، الأنْعامِ: ٥٣]، وذَكَرْنا مَعْنى الإشْراقِ فِي [الحِجْرِ: ٧٣] عِنْدَ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿مُشْرِقِينَ﴾. قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: الإشْراقُ: طُلُوعُ الشَّمْسِ [وإضاءَتُها]. ورُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ (p-١١١) أنَّهُ قالَ: طَلَبْتُ صَلاةَ الضُّحى، فَلَمْ أجِدْها إلّا فِي هَذِهِ الآيَةِ. وقَدْ ذَكَرْنا عَنْهُ أنَّ صَلاةَ الضُّحى مَذْكُورَةٌ فِي [النُّورِ: ٣٦] فِي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿بِالغُدُوِّ والآصالِ﴾.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿والطَّيْرَ مَحْشُورَةً﴾ وقَرَأ عِكْرِمَةُ، وأبُو الجَوْزاءِ، والضَّحّاكُ، وابْنُ أبِي عَبْلَةَ: "والطَّيْرُ مَحْشُورَةٌ" بِالرَّفْعِ فِيهِما، أيْ: مَجْمُوعَةٌ إلَيْهِ، تُسَبِّحُ اللَّهَ مَعَهُ. ﴿كُلٌّ لَهُ﴾ فِي هاءِ الكِنايَةِ قَوْلانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّها تَرْجِعُ إلى داوُدَ، أيْ: كُلٌّ لِداوُدَ ﴿أوّابٌ﴾ أيْ: رَجّاعٌ إلى طاعَتِهِ وأمْرِهِ، والمَعْنى: كُلٌّ لَهُ مُطِيعٌ بِالتَّسْبِيحِ مَعَهُ، هَذا قَوْلُ الجُمْهُورِ.

والثّانِي: [أنَّها] تَرْجِعُ إلى اللَّهِ تَعالى، فالمَعْنى: كُلٌّ مُسَبِّحٌ لِلَّهِ، قالَهُ السُّدِّيُّ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَشَدَدْنا مُلْكَهُ﴾ أيْ: قَوَّيْناهُ. وفِي ما شَدَّ بِهِ مُلْكَهُ قَوْلانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ الحَرَسُ والجُنُودُ؛ قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: كانَ يَحْرُسُهُ كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ سِتَّةٌ وثَلاثُونَ ألْفَ رَجُلٍ.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ هَيْبَةٌ أُلْقِيَتْ لَهُ فِي قُلُوبِ النّاسِ؛ وهَذا المَعْنى مَرْوِيٌّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أيْضًا.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَآتَيْناهُ الحِكْمَةَ﴾ وفِيها أرْبَعَةُ أقْوالٍ: أحَدُها: أنَّها الفَهْمُ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنُ، وابْنُ زَيْدٍ. والثّانِي: الصَّوابُ، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ. والثّالِثُ: السُّنَّةُ، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ. والرّابِعُ: النُّبُوَّةُ، قالَهُ السُّدِّيُّ.

وفِي فَصْلِ الخِطابِ أرْبَعَةُ أقْوالٍ.

أحَدُها: عِلْمُ القَضاءِ والعَدْلِ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنُ.

(p-١١٢) والثّانِي: بَيانُ الكَلامِ، رُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أيْضًا. وذَكَرَ الماوَرْدِيُّ أنَّهُ البَيانُ الكافِي فِي كُلِّ غَرَضٍ مَقْصُودٍ.

والثّالِثُ: قَوْلُ: "أمّا بَعْدُ"، وهو أوَّلُ مَن تَكَلَّمَ بِها، قالَهُ أبُو مُوسى الأشْعَرِيُّ، والشَّعْبِيُّ.

والرّابِعُ: تَكْلِيفُ المُدَّعِي البَيِّنَةَ، والمُدَّعى عَلَيْهِ اليَمِينَ، قالَهُ شُرَيْحٌ، وقَتادَةُ؛ وهو قَوْلٌ حَسَنٌ، لِأنَّ الخُصُومَةَ إنَّما تُفْصَلُ بِهَذا.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى ﴿وَقالُوا رَبَّنا عَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا﴾ فِي سَبَبِ قَوْلِهِمْ هَذا قَوْلانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ لَمّا ذَكَرَ لَهم ما فِي الجَنَّةِ، قالُوا هَذا، قالَهُ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ، والسُّدِّيُّ.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ لَمّا نَزَلَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَأمّا مَن أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ. . .﴾ الآياتُ [الحاقَّةِ: ١٩ ٣٧]، قالَتْ قُرَيْشٌ: زَعَمْتَ يا مُحَمَّدُ أنّا نُؤْتى كُتُبَنا بِشَمائِلِنا؟! فَعَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا، يَقُولُونَ ذَلِكَ تَكْذِيبًا لَهُ، قالَهُ أبُو العالِيَةِ، ومُقاتِلٌ.

وفِي المُرادِ بِالقِطِّ أرْبَعَةُ أقْوالٍ.

أحَدُها: أنَّهُ الصَّحِيفَةُ، قالَهُ أبُو صالِحٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ. قالَ الفَرّاءُ: القِطُّ (p-١٠٩) فِي كَلامِ العَرَبِ: الصَّكُّ. وقالَ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ: القِطُّ: الكِتابُ، والقُطُوطُ: الكُتُبُ بِالجَوائِزِ. وإلى هَذا المَعْنى ذَهَبَ الحَسَنُ، ومُقاتِلٌ، وابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ.

والثّانِي: أنَّ القِطَّ: الحِسابُ، رَواهُ الضَّحّاكُ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّهُ القَضاءُ، قالَهُ عَطاءٌ الخُراسانِيُّ، والمَعْنى أنَّهم لَمّا وُعِدُوا بِالقَضاءِ بَيْنَهُمْ، سَألُوا ذَلِكَ.

والرّابِعُ: أنَّهُ النَّصِيبُ، قالَهُ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ. [قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: القِطُّ: النَّصِيبُ، وأصْلُهُ: الصَّحِيفَةُ يُكْتَبُ لِلْإنْسانِ فِيها شَيْءٌ يَصِلُ إلَيْهِ، واشْتِقاقُهُ مِن قَطَطْتُ، أيْ: قَطَعْتُ، فالنَّصِيبُ: هو القِطْعَةُ مِنَ الشَّيْءِ. ثُمَّ فِي هَذا القَوْلِ لِلْمُفَسِّرِينَ قَوْلانِ. أحَدُهُما: أنَّهم سَألُوهُ نَصِيبَهم مِنَ الجَنَّةِ، قالَهُ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ.]

والثّانِي: سَألُوهُ نَصِيبَهم مِنَ العَذابِ، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ. وعَلى جَمِيعِ الأقْوالِ، إنَّما سَألُوا ذَلِكَ اسْتِهْزاءً بِتَكْذِيبِهِمْ بِالقِيامَةِ.

﴿اصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ﴾ أيْ: مِن تَكْذِيبِهِمْ وأذاهُمْ؛ وفِي هَذا قَوْلانِ.

(p-١١٠) أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ أمَرَ بِالصَّبْرِ، سُلُوكًا لِطَرِيقِ أُولِي العَزْمِ (أي الرسل أصحاب العزيمة)، وهَذا مُحْكَمٌ.

أحَدُها: عِلْمُ القَضاءِ والعَدْلِ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنُ.

(p-١١٢) والثّانِي: بَيانُ الكَلامِ، رُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أيْضًا. وذَكَرَ الماوَرْدِيُّ أنَّهُ البَيانُ الكافِي فِي كُلِّ غَرَضٍ مَقْصُودٍ.

والثّالِثُ: قَوْلُ: "أمّا بَعْدُ"، وهو أوَّلُ مَن تَكَلَّمَ بِها، قالَهُ أبُو مُوسى الأشْعَرِيُّ، والشَّعْبِيُّ.

والرّابِعُ: تَكْلِيفُ المُدَّعِي البَيِّنَةَ، والمُدَّعى عَلَيْهِ اليَمِينَ، قالَهُ شُرَيْحٌ، وقَتادَةُ؛ وهو قَوْلٌ حَسَنٌ، لِأنَّ الخُصُومَةَ إنَّما تُفْصَلُ بِهَذا.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى ﴿وَقالُوا رَبَّنا عَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا﴾ فِي سَبَبِ قَوْلِهِمْ هَذا قَوْلانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ لَمّا ذَكَرَ لَهم ما فِي الجَنَّةِ، قالُوا هَذا، قالَهُ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ، والسُّدِّيُّ.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ لَمّا نَزَلَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَأمّا مَن أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ. . .﴾ الآياتُ [الحاقَّةِ: ١٩ ٣٧]، قالَتْ قُرَيْشٌ: زَعَمْتَ يا مُحَمَّدُ أنّا نُؤْتى كُتُبَنا بِشَمائِلِنا؟! فَعَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا، يَقُولُونَ ذَلِكَ تَكْذِيبًا لَهُ، قالَهُ أبُو العالِيَةِ، ومُقاتِلٌ.

وفِي المُرادِ بِالقِطِّ أرْبَعَةُ أقْوالٍ.

أحَدُها: أنَّهُ الصَّحِيفَةُ، قالَهُ أبُو صالِحٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ. قالَ الفَرّاءُ: القِطُّ (p-١٠٩) فِي كَلامِ العَرَبِ: الصَّكُّ. وقالَ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ: القِطُّ: الكِتابُ، والقُطُوطُ: الكُتُبُ بِالجَوائِزِ. وإلى هَذا المَعْنى ذَهَبَ الحَسَنُ، ومُقاتِلٌ، وابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ.

والثّانِي: أنَّ القِطَّ: الحِسابُ، رَواهُ الضَّحّاكُ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّهُ القَضاءُ، قالَهُ عَطاءٌ الخُراسانِيُّ، والمَعْنى أنَّهم لَمّا وُعِدُوا بِالقَضاءِ بَيْنَهُمْ، سَألُوا ذَلِكَ.

والرّابِعُ: أنَّهُ النَّصِيبُ، قالَهُ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ. [قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: القِطُّ: النَّصِيبُ، وأصْلُهُ: الصَّحِيفَةُ يُكْتَبُ لِلْإنْسانِ فِيها شَيْءٌ يَصِلُ إلَيْهِ، واشْتِقاقُهُ مِن قَطَطْتُ، أيْ: قَطَعْتُ، فالنَّصِيبُ: هو القِطْعَةُ مِنَ الشَّيْءِ. ثُمَّ فِي هَذا القَوْلِ لِلْمُفَسِّرِينَ قَوْلانِ. أحَدُهُما: أنَّهم سَألُوهُ نَصِيبَهم مِنَ الجَنَّةِ، قالَهُ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ.]

والثّانِي: سَألُوهُ نَصِيبَهم مِنَ العَذابِ، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ. وعَلى جَمِيعِ الأقْوالِ، إنَّما سَألُوا ذَلِكَ اسْتِهْزاءً بِتَكْذِيبِهِمْ بِالقِيامَةِ.

﴿اصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ﴾ أيْ: مِن تَكْذِيبِهِمْ وأذاهُمْ؛ وفِي هَذا قَوْلانِ.

(p-١١٠) أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ أمَرَ بِالصَّبْرِ، سُلُوكًا لِطَرِيقِ أُولِي العَزْمِ (أي الرسل أصحاب العزيمة)، وهَذا مُحْكَمٌ.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ مَنسُوخٌ بِآيَةِ السَّيْفِ فِيما زَعَمَ الكَلْبِيُّ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿واذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا داوُدَ﴾ فِي وجْهِ المُناسَبَةِ بَيْنَ قَوْلِهِ: "اصْبِرْ" وبَيْنَ قَوْلِهِ: "واذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا داوُدَ" قَوْلانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ أُمِرَ أنْ يَتَقَوّى عَلى الصَّبْرِ بِذِكْرِ قُوَّةِ داوُدَ عَلى العِبادَةِ والطّاعَةِ.

والثّانِي: أنَّ المَعْنى: عَرَّفَهم أنَّ الأنْبِياءَ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلامُ -مَعَ طاعَتِهِمْ- كانُوا خائِفِينَ مِنِّي، هَذا داوُدُ مَعَ قُوَّتِهِ عَلى العِبادَةِ، لَمْ يَزَلْ باكِيًا مُسْتَغْفِرًا، فَكَيْفَ حالُهم مَعَ أفْعالِهِمْ؟!

فَأمّا قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ذا الأيْدِ﴾ فَقالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: هِيَ القُوَّةُ فِي العِبادَةِ. وفِي "الصَّحِيحَيْنِ" (الصحيحان: صحيحا البخاري ومسلم) مِن حَدِيثِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو قالَ: قالَ لِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ): «أحَبُّ الصِّيامِ إلى اللَّهِ صِيامُ داوُدَ، كانَ يَصُومُ يَوْمًا ويُفْطِرُ يَوْمًا، وأحَبُّ الصَّلاةِ إلى اللَّهِ صَلاةُ داوُدَ، كانَ يَنامُ نِصْفَ اللَّيْلِ ويَقُومُ ثُلُثَهُ ويَنامُ سُدُسَهُ».

وفِي الأوّابِ أقْوالٌ قَدْ ذَكَرْناها فِي [بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ: ٢٥].

﴿إنّا سَخَّرْنا الجِبالَ مَعَهُ يُسَبِّحْنَ﴾ قَدْ ذَكَرْنا تَسْبِيحَ الجِبالِ مَعَهُ فِي [الأنْبِياءِ: ٧٩]، وذَكَرْنا مَعْنى العَشِيِّ فِي مَواضِعَ مِمّا تَقَدَّمَ [آلِ عِمْرانَ: ٤١، الأنْعامِ: ٥٣]، وذَكَرْنا مَعْنى الإشْراقِ فِي [الحِجْرِ: ٧٣] عِنْدَ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿مُشْرِقِينَ﴾. قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: الإشْراقُ: طُلُوعُ الشَّمْسِ [وإضاءَتُها]. ورُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ (p-١١١) أنَّهُ قالَ: طَلَبْتُ صَلاةَ الضُّحى، فَلَمْ أجِدْها إلّا فِي هَذِهِ الآيَةِ. وقَدْ ذَكَرْنا عَنْهُ أنَّ صَلاةَ الضُّحى مَذْكُورَةٌ فِي [النُّورِ: ٣٦] فِي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿بِالغُدُوِّ والآصالِ﴾.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿والطَّيْرَ مَحْشُورَةً﴾ وقَرَأ عِكْرِمَةُ، وأبُو الجَوْزاءِ، والضَّحّاكُ، وابْنُ أبِي عَبْلَةَ: "والطَّيْرُ مَحْشُورَةٌ" بِالرَّفْعِ فِيهِما، أيْ: مَجْمُوعَةٌ إلَيْهِ، تُسَبِّحُ اللَّهَ مَعَهُ. ﴿كُلٌّ لَهُ﴾ فِي هاءِ الكِنايَةِ قَوْلانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّها تَرْجِعُ إلى داوُدَ، أيْ: كُلٌّ لِداوُدَ ﴿أوّابٌ﴾ أيْ: رَجّاعٌ إلى طاعَتِهِ وأمْرِهِ، والمَعْنى: كُلٌّ لَهُ مُطِيعٌ بِالتَّسْبِيحِ مَعَهُ، هَذا قَوْلُ الجُمْهُورِ.

والثّانِي: [أنَّها] تَرْجِعُ إلى اللَّهِ تَعالى، فالمَعْنى: كُلٌّ مُسَبِّحٌ لِلَّهِ، قالَهُ السُّدِّيُّ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَشَدَدْنا مُلْكَهُ﴾ أيْ: قَوَّيْناهُ. وفِي ما شَدَّ بِهِ مُلْكَهُ قَوْلانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ الحَرَسُ والجُنُودُ؛ قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: كانَ يَحْرُسُهُ كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ سِتَّةٌ وثَلاثُونَ ألْفَ رَجُلٍ.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ هَيْبَةٌ أُلْقِيَتْ لَهُ فِي قُلُوبِ النّاسِ؛ وهَذا المَعْنى مَرْوِيٌّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أيْضًا.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَآتَيْناهُ الحِكْمَةَ﴾ وفِيها أرْبَعَةُ أقْوالٍ: أحَدُها: أنَّها الفَهْمُ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنُ، وابْنُ زَيْدٍ. والثّانِي: الصَّوابُ، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ. والثّالِثُ: السُّنَّةُ، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ. والرّابِعُ: النُّبُوَّةُ، قالَهُ السُّدِّيُّ.

وفِي فَصْلِ الخِطابِ أرْبَعَةُ أقْوالٍ.

أحَدُها: عِلْمُ القَضاءِ والعَدْلِ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنُ.

(p-١١٢) والثّانِي: بَيانُ الكَلامِ، رُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أيْضًا. وذَكَرَ الماوَرْدِيُّ أنَّهُ البَيانُ الكافِي فِي كُلِّ غَرَضٍ مَقْصُودٍ.

والثّالِثُ: قَوْلُ: "أمّا بَعْدُ"، وهو أوَّلُ مَن تَكَلَّمَ بِها، قالَهُ أبُو مُوسى الأشْعَرِيُّ، والشَّعْبِيُّ.

والرّابِعُ: تَكْلِيفُ المُدَّعِي البَيِّنَةَ، والمُدَّعى عَلَيْهِ اليَمِينَ، قالَهُ شُرَيْحٌ، وقَتادَةُ؛ وهو قَوْلٌ حَسَنٌ، لِأنَّ الخُصُومَةَ إنَّما تُفْصَلُ بِهَذا.

﴿And has the news of the adversaries reached you?﴾ Abu Sulayman said: the meaning is, "It has indeed reached you, so listen to it. We shall relate it to you."

The scholars differed about the cause for which Dawud (peace be upon him) was tested, and they gave five opinions.

The first: he said, "My Lord, You have given Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub a remembrance (of You) such that I would have liked You to give me the same." Allah the Exalted said, "I tested them with what I did not test you with. If you wish, I will test you with the same test I gave them and give you what I gave them?" He said, "Yes." Then, while he was in his mihrab (the prayer chamber), a dove alighted upon him. He wished to take it, but it flew off. He went after it and saw a woman bathing. This was narrated by al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas, and al-Suddi also said so.

The second: he kept striving in worship until his companions from among the angels appeared to him. They used to pray with him and accompany him in weeping. When he grew comfortable with them, he said, "Tell me, what are you entrusted with?" They said, "We do not record any sin against you. Rather, we record your good deeds, make you steadfast, grant you success, and turn evil away from you." He said to himself, "I wonder how I would be if they left me and myself alone." He wished that he would be left between himself and himself so that he might know how he would be. So Allah the Exalted commanded his companions to withdraw from him, so that he would know that he has no independence from Allah [Mighty and Majestic]. When he lost them, he exerted himself and strove to double his worship, until he thought he had overcome his own self. Then Allah the Exalted [wished] to make him know his weakness, so He sent to him a bird from the birds of Paradise, which fell into his mihrab. He broke off his prayer and reached out his hand to it, but it moved away from its place. He followed it with his gaze, and behold, there was the wife of Uriah. This is the statement of Wahb ibn Munabbih.

The third: he and the Children of Israel discussed together, and they said, "Can there come upon a person a day in which he commits no sin?" Dawud resolved in himself that he would be able to do that. When the day of his worship came, he closed his doors, ordered that no one enter upon him, and devoted himself to reciting the Zabur (Psalms). Then there was a golden dove. He lunged at it, and it flew off. He followed it and saw the woman. This was narrated by Mattar from al-Hasan.

The fourth: when he became king, he said to the Children of Israel, "By Allah, I will surely be just among you," and he did not add the qualification (of God's will), so he was tested. This was narrated by Qatada from al-Hasan.

The fifth: he was impressed by the abundance of his deeds, so he was tested. This was said by Abu Bakr al-Warraq.

**The allusion to the story of his testing**

We have already mentioned from Wahb that he said: the dove was one of the birds of Paradise. al-Suddi said: Satan appeared to him in the form of a dove. The commentators said: when he followed the dove, he saw a woman in a garden by the edge of a pool of hers, bathing. It was also said: rather, on a roof of hers. He was amazed at her beauty (p-115), and she happened to glance and saw his shadow, so she loosened her hair, and it covered her body. This increased his admiration for her. He asked about her, and it was said, "This is the wife of Uriah, and her husband is on a military campaign." Dawud wrote to the commander of that army, "Send Uriah to such-and-such a place, and put him in front of the Ark." Whoever went in front of the Ark was not permitted to return until victory was granted to him or he was martyred. He did so, and victory came to him, so he wrote to Dawud informing him. Dawud wrote back, "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such," and he conquered for him. He wrote to Dawud informing him again, and Dawud wrote back, "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such." He was killed on the third occasion. When the woman's waiting period ended, Dawud married her, and she is the mother of Sulayman. When he consummated the marriage with her, he did not remain long before Allah the Mighty and Majestic sent two angels in the form of two men. It was also said: the two angels did not come to him until Sulayman had been born from her and had grown up. Then they came to him and found him in his prayer chamber of worship, but the guards prevented them from entering to him, so they climbed over the mihrab to him.

This story which we have mentioned is what most commentators hold. al-Awfi narrated something similar from Ibn Abbas, and it is related from al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Suddi, Muqatil and others.

A group of commentators mentioned that when Dawud looked at the woman, he asked about her and sent her husband to the military campaign again and again until he was killed, then he married her. Something like this [is] related from Ibn Abbas, Wahb, and al-Hasan along with a group. The author says: this is not sound by way of transmission, nor is it permissible in meaning, because prophets are free of such things.

The scholars (al-muhaqqiqun) differed about the sin for which he was rebuked, in four opinions.

The first: when he desired her, he said to her husband, "Transfer her to me," and so he was rebuked for that. Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Dawud did not go beyond saying to the woman's husband, "Entrust her to me and transfer her to me" (p-116). Something similar is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud. Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi related that he sent for Uriah and brought him back from his campaign, honored him greatly, until one day he said to him, "Step down for me from your wife, and look at whatever woman among the Children of Israel you wish, I will marry her to you, or whatever slave-girl you wish, I will buy her for you." He said, "I do not want any substitute for my wife." When he did not respond to what he asked, he ordered him to return to his campaign.

The second: he wished for that woman to be lawful for him, and he was inwardly disposed to that. Uriah's campaign and his death then happened by chance, without Dawud striving for the cause of his killing or exposing him to destruction. When news of his death reached him, he did not grieve over him as he grieved over others of his soldiers, then he married his wife, so he was rebuked for that. The sins of the prophets, peace be upon them, however small they may be, are great in the sight of Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

The third: when his gaze fell upon her, he gazed at her at length until she clung to his heart.

The fourth: Uriah had proposed to that woman, and Dawud proposed to her knowing that Uriah had proposed to her, and then married her. Uriah was distressed, and Allah the Exalted rebuked Dawud for not leaving her to her first suitor. Al-Qadi Abu Ya'la chose this opinion and supported it with the verse ﴿and he overpowered me in speech﴾. He said: this indicates that the exchange between them was only in the proposal, and the other man had not yet married her. So Dawud (peace be upon him) was rebuked for two things which the prophets should be free of: first, proposing over another man's proposal; second, showing eagerness to marry despite having many wives. He did not consider that a disobedience, so Allah the Exalted rebuked him for it. He said: as for what is related, that he looked at the woman, desired her, and sent her husband forward to be killed (p-117), this is a view which is not permissible for the prophets, because the prophets do not commit disobedience while knowing it is disobedience.

Al-Zajjaj said: He said "the adversary" (al-khasm) in the singular and said "they climbed over the mihrab" in the plural, because your saying khasm (adversary) is suitable for one, two, many, male and female. You say: this is a khasm, she is a khasm, they two are a khasm, and they are a khasm. It is suitable for all of that because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun): you say khasamtuhu akhsimuhu khasman. Here al-mihrab is like the upper chamber. The poet said:

*A lady of the mihrab, when you come to her, I do not reach her unless I climb a ladder.*

And "tasawwaru" (they climbed over) indicates height.

The commentators said: they were two angels. It was also said: they were Jibril and Mika'il (peace be upon them both), who came to him to alert him to repentance. He said "they climbed over" though they were two, because the meaning of plurality is the joining of one thing to another, and two or more constitute a group.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿when they entered upon Dawud﴾. Al-Farra' said: it is possible that the meaning of "tasawwaru" is "entered," so it would be a repetition. It is also possible that "idh" (when) has the meaning of "lamma" (when/after), so the meaning would be: when they climbed over the mihrab, after they entered, or when they climbed over, when they entered.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿so he was alarmed by them﴾. That is because they came in a manner not characteristic of people coming for litigation, and at a time not suited to judgment, and they entered by climbing over without permission. Abu al-Ahwas said: they entered upon him, each one of them taking hold of the other's head. The word ﴿two adversaries﴾ is in the nominative, with an implied "nahnu" (we). Ibn al-Anbari said: the meaning is: "We are like two adversaries, or like two adversaries," so the particle of comparison (ka) was dropped and the two adversaries took its place, as the Arabs say: "Abdullah is the moon in beauty," and they mean "like the moon." Hind bint Utba said in lamenting her father and her paternal uncle:

*From the sight of my two brothers, like two branches, or whoever saw them,*
*Two lions in a thicket, from whose lair the people shy away,*
*Two falcons that do not humble themselves, and whose sanctuary is not violated,*
*Two spears of Khatt in the heart of the sky, you see them.*

She meant "like two lions" and "like two falcons," so she dropped the word for "like" and put the word after it in its place. Then Allah the Mighty and Majestic turned the nun and alif in "ba'dina" (some of us) into the pronoun "nahnu" (we), as the Arabs say: "We are a people whose father has been honored," and "We are a people whose father of them has been honored," and the meaning is the same. Here "al-haqq" (the truth) means justice.

﴿and do not exceed the bounds﴾, i.e., do not act unjustly. It is said: shatta and ashatta, when he acted unjustly. Ibn Abi Abla recited "wa la tashtut" with a fatha on the ta' and a damma on the ta'. Al-Farra' said: some Arabs say "shatatta 'alayya fi al-sumum" (you exceeded against me in the poisons), but most of speech is "ashattat" with an alif. "Shattati al-dar" means the house became distant.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿and guide us to the even path﴾, i.e., to the middle of the road. The meaning is: bring us to the truth. Dawud said, "Speak." One of them said: ﴿Indeed, this is my brother﴾. Ibn al-Anbari said: the meaning is: one of the two adversaries, by whom the two angels were likened, said, "Indeed, this is my brother," and the saying was omitted because its meaning is clear. ﴿He has ninety-nine ewes﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the woman was referred to by the ewe. Others said: the Arabs liken women to ewes and allude to them by sheep and cattle. Ibn Qutayba said: he alluded to mention of women by mention of ewes, as 'Antara said:

*O ewe of the hunting ground, for whoever it is lawful for him, you are forbidden to me, and would that you were not forbidden.*

He alludes to a slave-girl, saying: what game are you for him for whom it is lawful to hunt you! As for me, the sanctity of the neighborhood has forbidden you to me. The king mentioned this number because it is the number of Dawud's wives.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿but I have only one ewe﴾. Hafs from 'Asim pronounced the ya' with a fatha, while the rest read it with sukun.

﴿So he said: "Entrust her to me"﴾. Ibn Qutayba said: i.e., include her with me and make me her guardian. Al-Zajjaj said: step down from her yourself and let me take charge of her.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿and he overpowered me in speech﴾, i.e., he overcame me in words. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Abu Razin [al-Uqayli], al-Dahhak, Ibn Ya'mur, and Ibn Abi Abla read "wa 'aznī" with an alif, meaning: he overcame me. Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas said concerning Allah's words "and he overpowered me in speech": he added nothing beyond saying, "Step down for me from her." al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: if you call and he calls, his will be greater; and if you strike and he strikes, his will be more severe than mine.

If it is asked: how did the two angels say this, when none of it was present with them?

The answer: the scholars said: this was only by way of example and comparison with the story of Dawud, and the sense of their speech is: "What would you say if two adversaries came to you and said such-and-such?" And Dawud did not consider that he bore any responsibility for what he had done, so Allah alerted him through the two angels. Ibn Qutayba said: this is a parable which Allah struck for him, alerting him to his error. We have already mentioned above that the meaning is: "We are like two adversaries."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He said﴾, meaning Dawud: ﴿He has certainly wronged you by demanding your ewe be added to his ewes﴾ (p-121).

Al-Farra' said: i.e., by his demand for your ewe. When you drop the ha' from "su'al" (demand), you attribute the verb to the ewe. Similar is Allah's words: ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good﴾ [Fussilat: 49], i.e., of asking for it with good. When he dropped the ha', he attributed the verb to "good," and dropped the ba' from "min al-khayr" (of good). They recited:

*So I will not be a greeter as long as I live, upon Zayd with a greeting of the commander.*

i.e., with a greeting upon the commander.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿to his ewes﴾, i.e., so that he might add her to his ewes. Ibn Qutayba said: the meaning is: by demanding your ewe joined to his ewes, and he abbreviated. He said: it is also said that "ila" (to) has the meaning of "ma'a" (with).

If the question is asked: how did Dawud (ﷺ) judge before hearing the words of the other party?
The answer: the other party had confessed, so he was judged on the basis of his confession. The mention of the confession was omitted, relying on the listener's understanding. The Arabs say: "I commanded you to trade, so you earned wealth," meaning: "so you traded and earned." What supports this is the statement of al-Suddi: Dawud said to the other party: "What do you say?" He said: "Yes, I want to take her from him to complete my ewes, while he is unwilling." He said: "Then we will not leave you alone; and if you insist on this, we will strike this part of you," pointing to his nose and forehead. He said: "You, O Dawud, are more deserving that this be struck from you, since you have ninety-nine wives, and Uriah had only one." Dawud looked and saw no one, and so he knew what he had fallen into.

His Exalted saying: ﴿And indeed, many of the associates (khulata')﴾, meaning the partners, singular khalit, who is one who mixes with another in property. He said this because he thought the two were partners. ﴿Except those who believe﴾ (p-122), meaning: they do not wrong anyone. ﴿And few are they﴾. "Ma" is superfluous, and the meaning is: "and few they are." It was also said: the meaning is: "they are few," meaning the righteous who do not wrong.

His Exalted saying: ﴿And Dawud thought﴾, meaning he became certain and knew, ﴿that We had tested him﴾. There are two views on this. One: We had tested him. The second: We had put him to trial by what occurred to him of looking at the woman and being tempted by her. Umar ibn al-Khattab recited "annama fatannahu" with the ta' and nun both doubled. Anas ibn Malik, Abu Razin, al-Hasan, Qatada, and Ali ibn Nasr from Abu Amr recited "annama fatanahu" with the ta' and nun both lightened, meaning the two angels. Abu Ali al-Farisi said: he means they confronted him. Regarding the cause of his knowledge and being alerted to this, there are three views.
One: the two angels made this clear to him, as we mentioned from al-Suddi.
The second: they ascended while saying: "The man has passed judgment against himself," so he knew that this was meant by it; this was said by Wahb.
The third: when he judged between them, one of them looked at his companion and laughed, then they ascended to the sky while he was watching, so he knew that Allah the Exalted had tested him with this; this was said by Muqatil.

His Exalted saying: ﴿So he sought forgiveness from his Lord﴾. The exegetes said: when Dawud became aware of his sin, he fell down bowing (rakti'an). Ibn Abbas said: meaning prostrating, and he expressed prostration by bowing, because both carry the sense of bending. Some said: the meaning is: he fell after having been bowing.

The scholars differed on whether this is one of the verses of prostration (aza'im al-sujud)? There are two views. One: it is not among the verses of prostration; this was said by al-Shafi'i. The second: it is among the verses of prostration; this was said by Abu Hanifa. From Ahmad there are two narrations. The exegetes said: he remained in his prostration for forty nights, not raising his head except for the time of an obligatory prayer or a necessary need, and he neither ate nor drank. The earth ate from his forehead, and grass grew from his tears, and he would say in his prostration: "Lord of Dawud, Dawud has slipped a slip farther than between East and West." Mujahid said: herbage grew from his tears until it covered his head; then he called out: "My Lord, my forehead has been wounded and my eye has dried up, and nothing has returned to him concerning his sin," so it was called to him: "Is it a hungry one that you may be fed, or a sick one that you may be healed, or an oppressed one that you may be defended?" Then he wept a weeping that stirred everything that had grown. At that moment He forgave him. Thabit al-Bunani said: Dawud took seven mattresses of hair, filled with ashes, then he wept until he poured them out with tears, and he did not drink any drink except mixed with the tears of his eyes. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: It was called out: "O Dawud, raise your head, for We have forgiven you," so he raised his head, and he had become weakened and trembling.

As for His saying: ﴿and he turned in repentance﴾, its meaning: he returned from his sin repentant to his Lord. ﴿So We forgave him that﴾, meaning the sin. ﴿And indeed for him with Us is a near station (zulfa)﴾ [Ibn Qutayba said]: meaning: advancement and nearness.

His Exalted saying: ﴿and a good final return﴾. Muqatil said: a good return, which is what Allah has prepared for him in Paradise.

His Exalted saying: ﴿O Dawud﴾, meaning: and We said to him: O Dawud, ﴿Indeed, We have made you﴾, meaning: We appointed you, ﴿a khalifa (successor) upon the earth﴾, meaning: you manage the affairs of the servants after Us by Our command, so it is as if you are a successor on Our behalf. ﴿So judge between the people with truth﴾, meaning: with justice. ﴿And do not follow desire﴾, meaning: do not incline toward what you desire when it contradicts the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿lest it lead you astray from the path of Allah﴾, meaning: from His religion. ﴿Indeed, those who go astray﴾. Abu Nahik, Abu Haywa, and Ibn Ya'mur recited "yadilluna" with a damma on the ya'.

His Exalted saying: ﴿for what they forgot of the Day of Account﴾. There are two views on this.
One: for what they neglected of works for the Day of Account; this was said by al-Suddi. Al-Zajjaj said: when they abandoned works for that day, they became like those who forget.
The second: in the speech there is advancement and delay; its meaning: for them is a severe punishment on the Day of Account because they forgot, that is, they abandoned judgment by justice; this is the view of Ikrima.

﴿And has the news of the adversaries reached you?﴾ Abu Sulayman said: the meaning is, "It has indeed reached you, so listen to it. We shall relate it to you."

The scholars differed about the cause for which Dawud (peace be upon him) was tested, and they gave five opinions.

The first: he said, "My Lord, You have given Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub a remembrance (of You) such that I would have liked You to give me the same." Allah the Exalted said, "I tested them with what I did not test you with. If you wish, I will test you with the same test I gave them and give you what I gave them?" He said, "Yes." Then, while he was in his mihrab (the prayer chamber), a dove alighted upon him. He wished to take it, but it flew off. He went after it and saw a woman bathing. This was narrated by al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas, and al-Suddi also said so.

The second: he kept striving in worship until his companions from among the angels appeared to him. They used to pray with him and accompany him in weeping. When he grew comfortable with them, he said, "Tell me, what are you entrusted with?" They said, "We do not record any sin against you. Rather, we record your good deeds, make you steadfast, grant you success, and turn evil away from you." He said to himself, "I wonder how I would be if they left me and myself alone." He wished that he would be left between himself and himself so that he might know how he would be. So Allah the Exalted commanded his companions to withdraw from him, so that he would know that he has no independence from Allah [Mighty and Majestic]. When he lost them, he exerted himself and strove to double his worship, until he thought he had overcome his own self. Then Allah the Exalted [wished] to make him know his weakness, so He sent to him a bird from the birds of Paradise, which fell into his mihrab. He broke off his prayer and reached out his hand to it, but it moved away from its place. He followed it with his gaze, and behold, there was the wife of Uriah. This is the statement of Wahb ibn Munabbih.

The third: he and the Children of Israel discussed together, and they said, "Can there come upon a person a day in which he commits no sin?" Dawud resolved in himself that he would be able to do that. When the day of his worship came, he closed his doors, ordered that no one enter upon him, and devoted himself to reciting the Zabur (Psalms). Then there was a golden dove. He lunged at it, and it flew off. He followed it and saw the woman. This was narrated by Mattar from al-Hasan.

The fourth: when he became king, he said to the Children of Israel, "By Allah, I will surely be just among you," and he did not add the qualification (of God's will), so he was tested. This was narrated by Qatada from al-Hasan.

The fifth: he was impressed by the abundance of his deeds, so he was tested. This was said by Abu Bakr al-Warraq.

**The allusion to the story of his testing**

We have already mentioned from Wahb that he said: the dove was one of the birds of Paradise. al-Suddi said: Satan appeared to him in the form of a dove. The commentators said: when he followed the dove, he saw a woman in a garden by the edge of a pool of hers, bathing. It was also said: rather, on a roof of hers. He was amazed at her beauty (p-115), and she happened to glance and saw his shadow, so she loosened her hair, and it covered her body. This increased his admiration for her. He asked about her, and it was said, "This is the wife of Uriah, and her husband is on a military campaign." Dawud wrote to the commander of that army, "Send Uriah to such-and-such a place, and put him in front of the Ark." Whoever went in front of the Ark was not permitted to return until victory was granted to him or he was martyred. He did so, and victory came to him, so he wrote to Dawud informing him. Dawud wrote back, "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such," and he conquered for him. He wrote to Dawud informing him again, and Dawud wrote back, "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such." He was killed on the third occasion. When the woman's waiting period ended, Dawud married her, and she is the mother of Sulayman. When he consummated the marriage with her, he did not remain long before Allah the Mighty and Majestic sent two angels in the form of two men. It was also said: the two angels did not come to him until Sulayman had been born from her and had grown up. Then they came to him and found him in his prayer chamber of worship, but the guards prevented them from entering to him, so they climbed over the mihrab to him.

This story which we have mentioned is what most commentators hold. al-Awfi narrated something similar from Ibn Abbas, and it is related from al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Suddi, Muqatil and others.

A group of commentators mentioned that when Dawud looked at the woman, he asked about her and sent her husband to the military campaign again and again until he was killed, then he married her. Something like this [is] related from Ibn Abbas, Wahb, and al-Hasan along with a group. The author says: this is not sound by way of transmission, nor is it permissible in meaning, because prophets are free of such things.

The scholars (al-muhaqqiqun) differed about the sin for which he was rebuked, in four opinions.

The first: when he desired her, he said to her husband, "Transfer her to me," and so he was rebuked for that. Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Dawud did not go beyond saying to the woman's husband, "Entrust her to me and transfer her to me" (p-116). Something similar is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud. Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi related that he sent for Uriah and brought him back from his campaign, honored him greatly, until one day he said to him, "Step down for me from your wife, and look at whatever woman among the Children of Israel you wish, I will marry her to you, or whatever slave-girl you wish, I will buy her for you." He said, "I do not want any substitute for my wife." When he did not respond to what he asked, he ordered him to return to his campaign.

The second: he wished for that woman to be lawful for him, and he was inwardly disposed to that. Uriah's campaign and his death then happened by chance, without Dawud striving for the cause of his killing or exposing him to destruction. When news of his death reached him, he did not grieve over him as he grieved over others of his soldiers, then he married his wife, so he was rebuked for that. The sins of the prophets, peace be upon them, however small they may be, are great in the sight of Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

The third: when his gaze fell upon her, he gazed at her at length until she clung to his heart.

The fourth: Uriah had proposed to that woman, and Dawud proposed to her knowing that Uriah had proposed to her, and then married her. Uriah was distressed, and Allah the Exalted rebuked Dawud for not leaving her to her first suitor. Al-Qadi Abu Ya'la chose this opinion and supported it with the verse ﴿and he overpowered me in speech﴾. He said: this indicates that the exchange between them was only in the proposal, and the other man had not yet married her. So Dawud (peace be upon him) was rebuked for two things which the prophets should be free of: first, proposing over another man's proposal; second, showing eagerness to marry despite having many wives. He did not consider that a disobedience, so Allah the Exalted rebuked him for it. He said: as for what is related, that he looked at the woman, desired her, and sent her husband forward to be killed (p-117), this is a view which is not permissible for the prophets, because the prophets do not commit disobedience while knowing it is disobedience.

Al-Zajjaj said: He said "the adversary" (al-khasm) in the singular and said "they climbed over the mihrab" in the plural, because your saying khasm (adversary) is suitable for one, two, many, male and female. You say: this is a khasm, she is a khasm, they two are a khasm, and they are a khasm. It is suitable for all of that because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun): you say khasamtuhu akhsimuhu khasman. Here al-mihrab is like the upper chamber. The poet said:

*A lady of the mihrab, when you come to her, I do not reach her unless I climb a ladder.*

And "tasawwaru" (they climbed over) indicates height.

The commentators said: they were two angels. It was also said: they were Jibril and Mika'il (peace be upon them both), who came to him to alert him to repentance. The scholars differed on whether this is one of the verses of prostration (aza'im al-sujud)? There are two views. One: it is not among the verses of prostration; this was said by al-Shafi'i. The second: it is among the verses of prostration; this was said by Abu Hanifa. From Ahmad there are two narrations. The exegetes said: he remained in his prostration for forty nights, not raising his head except for the time of an obligatory prayer or a necessary need, and he neither ate nor drank. The earth ate from his forehead, and grass grew from his tears, and he would say in his prostration: "Lord of Dawud, Dawud has slipped a slip farther than between East and West." Mujahid said: herbage grew from his tears until it covered his head; then he called out: "My Lord, my forehead has been wounded and my eye has dried up, and nothing has returned to him concerning his sin," so it was called to him: "Is it a hungry one that you may be fed, or a sick one that you may be healed, or an oppressed one that you may be defended?" Then he wept a weeping that stirred everything that had grown. At that moment He forgave him. Thabit al-Bunani said: Dawud took seven mattresses of hair, filled with ashes, then he wept until he poured them out with tears, and he did not drink any drink except mixed with the tears of his eyes. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: It was called out: "O Dawud, raise your head, for We have forgiven you," so he raised his head, and he had become weakened and trembling.

As for His saying: ﴿and he turned in repentance﴾, its meaning: he returned from his sin repentant to his Lord. ﴿So We forgave him that﴾, meaning the sin. ﴿And indeed for him with Us is a near station (zulfa)﴾ [Ibn Qutayba said]: meaning: advancement and nearness.

His Exalted saying: ﴿and a good final return﴾. Muqatil said: a good return, which is what Allah has prepared for him in Paradise.

His Exalted saying: ﴿O Dawud﴾, meaning: and We said to him: O Dawud, ﴿Indeed, We have made you﴾, meaning: We appointed you, ﴿a khalifa (successor) upon the earth﴾, meaning: you manage the affairs of the servants after Us by Our command, so it is as if you are a successor on Our behalf. ﴿So judge between the people with truth﴾, meaning: with justice. ﴿And do not follow desire﴾, meaning: do not incline toward what you desire when it contradicts the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿lest it lead you astray from the path of Allah﴾, meaning: from His religion. ﴿Indeed, those who go astray﴾. Abu Nahik, Abu Haywa, and Ibn Ya'mur recited "yadilluna" with a damma on the ya'.

His Exalted saying: ﴿for what they forgot of the Day of Account﴾. There are two views on this.
One: for what they neglected of works for the Day of Account; this was said by al-Suddi. Al-Zajjaj said: when they abandoned works for that day, they became like those who forget.
The second: in the speech there is advancement and delay; its meaning: for them is a severe punishment on the Day of Account because they forgot, that is, they abandoned judgment by justice; this is the view of Ikrima.

﴿And has the news of the adversaries reached you?﴾ Abu Sulayman said: the meaning is, "It has indeed reached you, so listen to it. We shall relate it to you."

The scholars differed about the cause for which Dawud (peace be upon him) was tested, and they gave five opinions.

The first: he said, "My Lord, You have given Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub a remembrance (of You) such that I would have liked You to give me the same." Allah the Exalted said, "I tested them with what I did not test you with. If you wish, I will test you with the same test I gave them and give you what I gave them?" He said, "Yes." Then, while he was in his mihrab (the prayer chamber), a dove alighted upon him. He wished to take it, but it flew off. He went after it and saw a woman bathing. This was narrated by al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas, and al-Suddi also said so.

The second: he kept striving in worship until his companions from among the angels appeared to him. They used to pray with him and accompany him in weeping. When he grew comfortable with them, he said, "Tell me, what are you entrusted with?" They said, "We do not record any sin against you. Rather, we record your good deeds, make you steadfast, grant you success, and turn evil away from you." He said to himself, "I wonder how I would be if they left me and myself alone." He wished that he would be left between himself and himself so that he might know how he would be. So Allah the Exalted commanded his companions to withdraw from him, so that he would know that he has no independence from Allah [Mighty and Majestic]. When he lost them, he exerted himself and strove to double his worship, until he thought he had overcome his own self. Then Allah the Exalted [wished] to make him know his weakness, so He sent to him a bird from the birds of Paradise, which fell into his mihrab. He broke off his prayer and reached out his hand to it, but it moved away from its place. He followed it with his gaze, and behold, there was the wife of Uriah. This is the statement of Wahb ibn Munabbih.

The third: he and the Children of Israel discussed together, and they said, "Can there come upon a person a day in which he commits no sin?" Dawud resolved in himself that he would be able to do that. When the day of his worship came, he closed his doors, ordered that no one enter upon him, and devoted himself to reciting the Zabur (Psalms). Then there was a golden dove. He lunged at it, and it flew off. He followed it and saw the woman. This was narrated by Mattar from al-Hasan.

The fourth: when he became king, he said to the Children of Israel, "By Allah, I will surely be just among you," and he did not add the qualification (of God's will), so he was tested. This was narrated by Qatada from al-Hasan.

The fifth: he was impressed by the abundance of his deeds, so he was tested. This was said by Abu Bakr al-Warraq.

**The allusion to the story of his testing**

We have already mentioned from Wahb that he said: the dove was one of the birds of Paradise. al-Suddi said: Satan appeared to him in the form of a dove. The commentators said: when he followed the dove, he saw a woman in a garden by the edge of a pool of hers, bathing. It was also said: rather, on a roof of hers. He was amazed at her beauty (p-115), and she happened to glance and saw his shadow, so she loosened her hair, and it covered her body. This increased his admiration for her. He asked about her, and it was said, "This is the wife of Uriah, and her husband is on a military campaign." Dawud wrote to the commander of that army, "Send Uriah to such-and-such a place, and put him in front of the Ark." Whoever went in front of the Ark was not permitted to return until victory was granted to him or he was martyred. He did so, and victory came to him, so he wrote to Dawud informing him. Dawud wrote back, "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such," and he conquered for him. He wrote to Dawud informing him again, and Dawud wrote back, "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such." He was killed on the third occasion. When the woman's waiting period ended, Dawud married her, and she is the mother of Sulayman. When he consummated the marriage with her, he did not remain long before Allah the Mighty and Majestic sent two angels in the form of two men. It was also said: the two angels did not come to him until Sulayman had been born from her and had grown up. Then they came to him and found him in his prayer chamber of worship, but the guards prevented them from entering to him, so they climbed over the mihrab to him.

This story which we have mentioned is what most commentators hold. al-Awfi narrated something similar from Ibn Abbas, and it is related from al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Suddi, Muqatil and others.

A group of commentators mentioned that when Dawud looked at the woman, he asked about her and sent her husband to the military campaign again and again until he was killed, then he married her. Something like this [is] related from Ibn Abbas, Wahb, and al-Hasan along with a group. The author says: this is not sound by way of transmission, nor is it permissible in meaning, because prophets are free of such things.

The scholars (al-muhaqqiqun) differed about the sin for which he was rebuked, in four opinions.

The first: when he desired her, he said to her husband, "Transfer her to me," and so he was rebuked for that. Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Dawud did not go beyond saying to the woman's husband, "Entrust her to me and transfer her to me" (p-116). Something similar is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud. Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi related that he sent for Uriah and brought him back from his campaign, honored him greatly, until one day he said to him, "Step down for me from your wife, and look at whatever woman among the Children of Israel you wish, I will marry her to you, or whatever slave-girl you wish, I will buy her for you." He said, "I do not want any substitute for my wife." When he did not respond to what he asked, he ordered him to return to his campaign.

The second: he wished for that woman to be lawful for him, and he was inwardly disposed to that. Uriah's campaign and his death then happened by chance, without Dawud striving for the cause of his killing or exposing him to destruction. When news of his death reached him, he did not grieve over him as he grieved over others of his soldiers, then he married his wife, so he was rebuked for that. The sins of the prophets, peace be upon them, however small they may be, are great in the sight of Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

The third: when his gaze fell upon her, he gazed at her at length until she clung to his heart.

The fourth: Uriah had proposed to that woman, and Dawud proposed to her knowing that Uriah had proposed to her, and then married her. Uriah was distressed, and Allah the Exalted rebuked Dawud for not leaving her to her first suitor. Al-Qadi Abu Ya'la chose this opinion and supported it with the verse ﴿and he overpowered me in speech﴾. He said: this indicates that the exchange between them was only in the proposal, and the other man had not yet married her. So Dawud (peace be upon him) was rebuked for two things which the prophets should be free of: first, proposing over another man's proposal; second, showing eagerness to marry despite having many wives. He did not consider that a disobedience, so Allah the Exalted rebuked him for it. He said: as for what is related, that he looked at the woman, desired her, and sent her husband forward to be killed (p-117), this is a view which is not permissible for the prophets, because the prophets do not commit disobedience while knowing it is disobedience.

Al-Zajjaj said: He said "the adversary" (al-khasm) in the singular and said "they climbed over the mihrab" in the plural, because your saying khasm (adversary) is suitable for one, two, many, male and female. You say: this is a khasm, she is a khasm, they two are a khasm, and they are a khasm. It is suitable for all of that because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun): you say khasamtuhu akhsimuhu khasman. Here al-mihrab is like the upper chamber. The poet said:

*A lady of the mihrab, when you come to her, I do not reach her unless I climb a ladder.*

And "tasawwaru" (they climbed over) indicates height.

The commentators said: they were two angels. It was also said: they were Jibril and Mika'il (peace be upon them both), who came to him to alert him to repentance. He said "they climbed over" though they were two, because the meaning of plurality is the joining of one thing to another, and two or more constitute a group.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿when they entered upon Dawud﴾. Al-Farra' said: it is possible that the meaning of "tasawwaru" is "entered," so it would be a repetition. It is also possible that "idh" (when) has the meaning of "lamma" (when/after), so the meaning would be: when they climbed over the mihrab, after they entered, or when they climbed over, when they entered.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿so he was alarmed by them﴾. That is because they came in a manner not characteristic of people coming for litigation, and at a time not suited to judgment, and they entered by climbing over without permission. Abu al-Ahwas said: they entered upon him, each one of them taking hold of the other's head. The word ﴿two adversaries﴾ is in the nominative, with an implied "nahnu" (we). Ibn al-Anbari said: the meaning is: "We are like two adversaries, or like two adversaries," so the particle of comparison (ka) was dropped and the two adversaries took its place, as the Arabs say: "Abdullah is the moon in beauty," and they mean "like the moon." Hind bint Utba said in lamenting her father and her paternal uncle:

*From the sight of my two brothers, like two branches, or whoever saw them,*
*Two lions in a thicket, from whose lair the people shy away,*
*Two falcons that do not humble themselves, and whose sanctuary is not violated,*
*Two spears of Khatt in the heart of the sky, you see them.*

She meant "like two lions" and "like two falcons," so she dropped the word for "like" and put the word after it in its place. Then Allah the Mighty and Majestic turned the nun and alif in "ba'dina" (some of us) into the pronoun "nahnu" (we), as the Arabs say: "We are a people whose father has been honored," and "We are a people whose father of them has been honored," and the meaning is the same. Here "al-haqq" (the truth) means justice.

﴿and do not exceed the bounds﴾, i.e., do not act unjustly. It is said: shatta and ashatta, when he acted unjustly. Ibn Abi Abla recited "wa la tashtut" with a fatha on the ta' and a damma on the ta'. Al-Farra' said: some Arabs say "shatatta 'alayya fi al-sumum" (you exceeded against me in the poisons), but most of speech is "ashattat" with an alif. "Shattati al-dar" means the house became distant.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿and guide us to the even path﴾, i.e., to the middle of the road. The meaning is: bring us to the truth. Dawud said, "Speak." One of them said: ﴿Indeed, this is my brother﴾. Ibn al-Anbari said: the meaning is: one of the two adversaries, by whom the two angels were likened, said, "Indeed, this is my brother," and the saying was omitted because its meaning is clear. ﴿He has ninety-nine ewes﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the woman was referred to by the ewe. Others said: the Arabs liken women to ewes and allude to them by sheep and cattle. Ibn Qutayba said: he alluded to mention of women by mention of ewes, as 'Antara said:

*O ewe of the hunting ground, for whoever it is lawful for him, you are forbidden to me, and would that you were not forbidden.*

He alludes to a slave-girl, saying: what game are you for him for whom it is lawful to hunt you! As for me, the sanctity of the neighborhood has forbidden you to me. The king mentioned this number because it is the number of Dawud's wives.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿but I have only one ewe﴾. Hafs from 'Asim pronounced the ya' with a fatha, while the rest read it with sukun.

﴿So he said: "Entrust her to me"﴾. Ibn Qutayba said: i.e., include her with me and make me her guardian. Al-Zajjaj said: step down from her yourself and let me take charge of her.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿and he overpowered me in speech﴾, i.e., he overcame me in words. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Abu Razin [al-Uqayli], al-Dahhak, Ibn Ya'mur, and Ibn Abi Abla read "wa 'aznī" with an alif, meaning: he overcame me. Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas said concerning Allah's words "and he overpowered me in speech": he added nothing beyond saying, "Step down for me from her." al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: if you call and he calls, his will be greater; and if you strike and he strikes, his will be more severe than mine.

If it is asked: how did the two angels say this, when none of it was present with them?

The answer: the scholars said: this was only by way of example and comparison with the story of Dawud, and the sense of their speech is: "What would you say if two adversaries came to you and said such-and-such?" And Dawud did not consider that he bore any responsibility for what he had done, so Allah alerted him through the two angels. Ibn Qutayba said: this is a parable which Allah struck for him, alerting him to his error. We have already mentioned above that the meaning is: "We are like two adversaries."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He said﴾, meaning Dawud: ﴿He has certainly wronged you by demanding your ewe be added to his ewes﴾ (p-121).

Al-Farra' said: i.e., by his demand for your ewe. When you drop the ha' from "su'al" (demand), you attribute the verb to the ewe. Similar is Allah's words: ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good﴾ [Fussilat: 49], i.e., of asking for it with good. When he dropped the ha', he attributed the verb to "good," and dropped the ba' from "min al-khayr" (of good). They recited:

*So I will not be a greeter as long as I live, upon Zayd with a greeting of the commander.*

i.e., with a greeting upon the commander.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿to his ewes﴾, i.e., so that he might add her to his ewes. Ibn Qutayba said: the meaning is: by demanding your ewe joined to his ewes, and he abbreviated. He said: it is also said that "ila" (to) has the meaning of "ma'a" (with).

If the question is asked: how did Dawud (ﷺ) judge before hearing the words of the other party?
The answer: the other party had confessed, so he was judged on the basis of his confession. The mention of the confession was omitted, relying on the listener's understanding. The Arabs say: "I commanded you to trade, so you earned wealth," meaning: "so you traded and earned." What supports this is the statement of al-Suddi: Dawud said to the other party: "What do you say?" He said: "Yes, I want to take her from him to complete my ewes, while he is unwilling." He said: "Then we will not leave you alone; and if you insist on this, we will strike this part of you," pointing to his nose and forehead. He said: "You, O Dawud, are more deserving that this be struck from you, since you have ninety-nine wives, and Uriah had only one." Dawud looked and saw no one, and so he knew what he had fallen into.

His Exalted saying: ﴿And indeed, many of the associates (khulata')﴾, meaning the partners, singular khalit, who is one who mixes with another in property. He said this because he thought the two were partners. ﴿Except those who believe﴾ (p-122), meaning: they do not wrong anyone. ﴿And few are they﴾. "Ma" is superfluous, and the meaning is: "and few they are." It was also said: the meaning is: "they are few," meaning the righteous who do not wrong.

His Exalted saying: ﴿And Dawud thought﴾, meaning he became certain and knew, ﴿that We had tested him﴾. There are two views on this. One: We had tested him. The second: We had put him to trial by what occurred to him of looking at the woman and being tempted by her. Umar ibn al-Khattab recited "annama fatannahu" with the ta' and nun both doubled. Anas ibn Malik, Abu Razin, al-Hasan, Qatada, and Ali ibn Nasr from Abu Amr recited "annama fatanahu" with the ta' and nun both lightened, meaning the two angels. Abu Ali al-Farisi said: he means they confronted him. Regarding the cause of his knowledge and being alerted to this, there are three views.
One: the two angels made this clear to him, as we mentioned from al-Suddi.
The second: they ascended while saying: "The man has passed judgment against himself," so he knew that this was meant by it; this was said by Wahb.
The third: when he judged between them, one of them looked at his companion and laughed, then they ascended to the sky while he was watching, so he knew that Allah the Exalted had tested him with this; this was said by Muqatil.

His Exalted saying: ﴿So he sought forgiveness from his Lord﴾. The exegetes said: when Dawud became aware of his sin, he fell down bowing (rakti'an). Ibn Abbas said: meaning prostrating, and he expressed prostration by bowing, because both carry the sense of bending. Some said: the meaning is: he fell after having been bowing.

When he lost them, he exerted himself and strove to double his worship, until he thought he had overcome his own self. Then Allah the Exalted [wished] to make him know his weakness, so He sent to him a bird from the birds of Paradise, which fell into his mihrab. He broke off his prayer and reached out his hand to it, but it moved away from its place. He followed it with his gaze, and behold, there was the wife of Uriah.
